title: Block 1 Checkpoint
subtitle: Orientation · Checkpoint
tagline: You've met the crew. Now prove it. Twelve checkpoints on team structure, roles, speeches, prep time, and the shape of a round.

slides.headline: Time to {{cyan: lock it in}}, debater.
body: You've completed Block 1 — you know the crew, the speeches, and the shape of a round. This mission is your **systems check**.
Twelve questions. About fifteen minutes. Most debaters clear it at **80% or higher**. Take your time, read each prompt, and trust what you learned.

quote.text: Don't rush. Every question maps to something Commander K showed you on the bridge. If you slow down, the answer is already in your head.

prompt.label: PICK ALL THAT APPLY
prompt.scenario: Commander K just showed you the full bridge of debaters in action.
prompt.question: Which of these statements are **TRUE** about policy debate?

options.text: Policy debate is a team activity played **2-on-2** (two debaters per side).
Each debater debates solo against one opponent.
The **Affirmative** team argues *for* a change, and the **Negative** team argues *against* it.
Every debater on the team gets a chance to speak and ask questions.
Only the strongest debater on each team gets to speak.

correct.title: ✓ TARGET ACQUIRED
body: You nailed the fundamentals. **Two on two. Everyone plays. Aff vs. Neg.** That's the whole shape.
correct.followup: Memory hook: nobody flies solo, nobody sits out.

wrongDefault.title: ✕ MISFIRE — RECALIBRATE
body: Three truths to lock in: policy debate is always **2-on-2**, *every* debater speaks and runs cross-ex, and the two sides are **Aff** (yes, change it) and **Neg** (no, don't).

prompt.label: TWO CHANCES TO SPEAK
prompt.question: Every debater gives **two** speeches per round. Which statements describe that pair of speeches correctly?

options.text: A **constructive** speech (where you build your case) and a **rebuttal** speech (where you respond and finish).
A constructive speech and **two** rebuttal speeches.
**Three** speeches total — constructive, rebuttal, and a closing.
One first speech (**constructive**) and one second speech (**rebuttal**).

correct.title: ✓ TARGET ACQUIRED
body: Right. **You speak twice: first to build, second to finish.** That's it. No closing speech, no third turn.
correct.followup: Memory hook: Constructive = *build it.* Rebuttal = *finish it.*

wrongDefault.title: ✕ MISFIRE — RECALIBRATE
body: Each debater gets exactly **two** speeches: **constructive** (build your case) and **rebuttal** (respond and finish). That's *your* two chances — no more, no less.

prompt.label: EXPLAIN IT TO YOUR FAMILY
prompt.scenario: Your mom asks, *"What's this policy debate thing?"* You want to give her a one-sentence analogy.
prompt.question: Which comparison **best** captures what policy debate is?

options.text: *"It's like a spelling bee — one person at a time, knocked out if they get it wrong."*
*"It's like doubles tennis — you have a partner, and two teams face off, taking turns."*
*"It's like watching a movie — you just sit and listen."*
*"It's like a track race — everyone runs alone and the fastest wins."*

correct.title: ✓ TARGET ACQUIRED
body: Doubles tennis is the cleanest analogy: **partner + team-vs-team + taking turns**. A co-op video game raid or a 2-on-2 basketball game would work too.
correct.followup: If anyone ever asks, lead with the partner. That's the part most people don't expect.

a.title: ✕ MISFIRE — RECALIBRATE
body: Spelling bees are **solo elimination**. Debate is **team vs. team**, with everyone speaking every round. Big difference.

c.title: ✕ MISFIRE — RECALIBRATE
body: Debate is the opposite of passive. *You* speak, *you* ask questions, *you* think under pressure. Doubles tennis is a closer fit.

d.title: ✕ MISFIRE — RECALIBRATE
body: The whole point of policy debate is that you **don't** fly solo. You're on a 2-person team. Try doubles tennis or a co-op video game raid.

wrongDefault.title: ✕ MISFIRE — RECALIBRATE
body: The best analogies share three traits with policy debate: **a partner, two teams, and taking turns**. Doubles tennis fits perfectly.

prompt.label: THE SHARED CLOCK
prompt.scenario: Your team has **8 minutes** of prep time before your first speech.
prompt.question: How does that prep time work?

options.text: You get 4 minutes solo + your partner gets 4 minutes solo, no overlap.
You and your partner **decide together** how to split or use all 8 minutes as a team.
The first speaker gets all 8 minutes; the second speaker gets none.
You use as much time as you want — there's no actual limit.

correct.title: ✓ TARGET ACQUIRED
body: Perfect. Prep time is a **shared bank**. You and your partner pilot it together — just like a timeout in basketball.
correct.followup: Tactical note: prep is one of the few things in a round you fully control. Spend it on purpose.

a.title: ✕ MISFIRE — RECALIBRATE
body: Prep isn't pre-split. It's **one shared bank** of 8–10 minutes that you and your partner allocate together.

c.title: ✕ MISFIRE — RECALIBRATE
body: Both speakers can use prep — it's shared. If the 1A burns all 8 minutes, the 2A has zero. That's a *choice*, not a rule.

d.title: ✕ MISFIRE — RECALIBRATE
body: There **is** a limit. Usually 8 or 10 minutes total per team for the whole round. When the bank hits zero, you're done.

wrongDefault.title: ✕ MISFIRE — RECALIBRATE
body: Prep time belongs to the **team**, not one person. You and your partner share 8–10 minutes total and decide together when to spend it.

prompt.label: THE QUESTION GAME
prompt.question: Which of these are **TRUE** about cross-examination (cross-ex)?

options.text: Every debater gets **3 minutes** to ask questions and **3 minutes** to answer questions.
Cross-ex happens after each **constructive** speech.
Only the strongest debater on the team asks questions.
When the other team is asking you questions, **you have to answer** — you can't skip your turn.
You can prepare your answers to specific questions before cross-ex starts.

correct.title: ✓ TARGET ACQUIRED
body: Solid. **3 minutes asking, 3 minutes answering**, after every constructive, no skipping. Cross-ex is built into the round.
correct.followup: Tactical note: cross-ex is when you set up your rebuttal. Listen for what they *can't* defend.

wrongDefault.title: ✕ MISFIRE — RECALIBRATE
body: Three locks on cross-ex: **everyone takes a turn**, it happens **after each constructive** (not just one), and you **can't predict** the questions in advance. It's live.

prompt.label: MATCH THE TERMS
prompt.question: Match each **term** from Block 1 to its **definition**.

items.text: A **shared bank** of 8–10 minutes your team uses to think between speeches.
**Everyone** from your school or program — bigger than just your team.
Your **second** speech — where you respond and finish strong.
Your **first** speech — where you build your case and arguments.
The 3-minute window where you **ask the other team questions** (or answer theirs).

correct.title: ✓ TARGET ACQUIRED
body: Vocab locked. You own the Mission Glossary: **Constructive** = first/build. **Rebuttal** = second/respond. **Cross-ex** = Q&A. **Prep** = shared bank. **Squad** = everyone.
correct.followup: Tactical note: these five words will appear in every single round you ever debate. Memorize them now.

wrongDefault.title: ✕ MISFIRE — RECALIBRATE
body: Re-align the easy mix-up: **Constructive is your FIRST speech** (you build). **Rebuttal is your SECOND speech** (you respond). The two often get flipped — but the order is constructive *then* rebuttal.

prompt.label: THE BIG PICTURE
prompt.question: Which of these are **TRUE** about a typical ~90-minute policy debate round?

options.text: The **Affirmative** team speaks first (1AC — First Affirmative Constructive).
After each constructive speech, there is a **cross-examination** period.
**Rebuttals** happen after **all** constructive speeches are done.
Every speech is the **same length** (all 8 minutes).
The **Negative** team gets the **last speech** (2NR — Second Negative Rebuttal).

correct.title: ✓ TARGET ACQUIRED
body: You see the **whole structure**. **AFF opens, everyone takes turns, all constructives come before any rebuttals, and NEG closes.** That's the shape of every round.
correct.followup: Memory hook: Aff first. Neg last. Constructives before rebuttals. Cross-ex in between.

d.title: ✕ MISFIRE — RECALIBRATE
body: Speech lengths **vary** — constructives are longer than rebuttals. You'll drill the exact times in Block 2.

wrongDefault.title: ✕ MISFIRE — RECALIBRATE
body: Lock in the order: **1AC → cross-ex → 1NC → cross-ex → 2AC → cross-ex → 2NC → cross-ex**, then all rebuttals. **Aff opens. Neg closes.** Speech lengths are not equal.

slides.headline: BLOCK 1 CLEARED
slides.subtext: Twelve checkpoints. Team structure, roles, speeches, prep time, cross-ex, the shape of a round — all of it locked in. You're cleared for Block 2.
